name: Sabarmati Ashram (Gandhi Ashram)
description: Riverside ashram that was Mahatma Gandhi's home and base from 1917 to 1930, from where he set out on the Salt March. Its museum, the Gandhi Smarak Sangrahalaya designed by Charles Correa, holds a large archive of books, letters and photographs, alongside Gandhi's cottage Hriday Kunj.
address: Ashram Road, Sabarmati, Ahmedabad (on the Sabarmati riverbank)

name: Sidi Saiyyed Mosque
description: Mosque completed in 1572-73 by Sidi Saiyyed, a nobleman of African descent at the Gujarat Sultanate court. It is famous for its carved stone jali windows showing an intertwined tree of life, an unofficial symbol of Ahmedabad.
address: Near Lal Darwaja, Ahmedabad

name: Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad
description: The city's main Friday mosque, built by Sultan Ahmad Shah I and completed in 1424 in yellow sandstone. Its prayer hall has around 260 columns supporting 15 domes, facing a large marble-paved courtyard with an ablution tank.
address: Gandhi Road, near Teen Darwaza, old walled city

name: Bhadra Fort
description: Citadel founded by Ahmad Shah I in 1411 as the core of the new city, named after the Bhadra Kali temple inside. Its surviving gates and walls were restored under the Bhadra Plaza project completed in 2014, and the rooftop gives views over the old city.
address: Bhadra, walled city, east bank of the Sabarmati

name: Teen Darwaza
description: Triple-arched royal gateway built by Ahmad Shah I and completed in 1415, once leading to the fort's outer court. It carries a 1812 Maratha-era inscription granting daughters inheritance rights and sits in one of the old city's busiest street markets.
address: East of Bhadra Fort, old walled city

name: Adalaj Stepwell (Adalaj ni Vav)
description: Five-storey sandstone stepwell from 1498-99 in Adalaj village north of Ahmedabad, credited to Queen Rudabai and finished under Mahmud Begada. Its octagonal shaft and pillars are richly carved with Hindu, Jain and Islamic motifs, and the interior stays noticeably cooler than outside.
address: Adalaj village, Gandhinagar district (about 19 km north of Ahmedabad)

name: Dada Harir Stepwell (Bai Harir ni Vav)
description: Five-storey sandstone stepwell in Asarwa built around 1499-1500 for Bai Harir Sultani, superintendent of Sultan Mahmud Begada's harem, together with a mosque and her tomb. It has an octagonal shaft, carved pillars and elephant motifs.
address: Asarwa, Ahmedabad

name: Hutheesing Jain Temple
description: White-marble Shvetambara Jain temple opened in 1848, dedicated to Dharmanath, the 15th tirthankara. Begun by merchant Hathisinh Kesarisinh and completed by his widow Harkunvar, it has 52 subsidiary shrines around its courtyard and a tall Manastambha tower.
address: Delhi Darwaja - Shahibaug Road, Bardolpura, Delhi Darwaza, Ahmedabad

name: Sarkhej Roza
description: Mosque, tomb and palace complex around a large tank at Makarba, built around the tomb of Sufi saint Shaikh Ahmed Khattu Ganj Bakhsh (finished 1451) and extended by Mahmud Begada. Le Corbusier likened its composition to the Acropolis.
address: Makarba, Post Jeevraj Park, Ahmedabad 380051

name: Rani no Hajiro (Queen's Mausoleum)
description: Raised, cloistered enclosure from around 1445 holding the marble tombs of queens of the Gujarat Sultanate, including Mughlai Bibi. Its courtyard is now a busy market for women's clothing, jewellery and accessories near Manek Chowk.
address: Manek Chowk, old walled city

name: Badshah no Hajiro (Ahmed Shah's Tomb)
description: Domed mausoleum of Sultan Ahmad Shah I, founder of Ahmedabad, beside the Jama Masjid; his son and grandson are buried with him. Corner chambers have carved stone jalis, and a traditional naubat band still plays here daily.
address: Near Manek Chowk, next to Jama Masjid

name: Jhulta Minar (Sidi Bashir Mosque)
description: Pair of three-storey carved minarets, the surviving gateway of the Sidi Bashir Mosque near Sarangpur Darwaja. Shaking one minaret makes the other vibrate while the connecting passage stays still; demonstrations are no longer held.
address: Opposite Sarangpur Darwaja, north of Ahmedabad Junction railway station

name: Rani Sipri Mosque (Masjid-e-Nagina)
description: Small mosque and tomb built in 1514 by Rani Sipri, a queen of Sultan Mahmud Begada, who is buried here. Known as the 'jewel of a mosque' for its delicate jali screens with plant motifs and its slender minarets.
address: Near Astodia Gate, old walled city

name: Shree Swaminarayan Mandir, Kalupur
description: The first temple of the Swaminarayan Sampraday, inaugurated in 1822, known for its colourful carved Burma-teak woodwork and a gateway mixing local and colonial styles. The city's daily morning heritage walk starts here.
address: Swaminarayan Mandir Road, Kalupur, Ahmedabad 380001

name: Ahmed Shah's Mosque
description: The oldest mosque in Ahmedabad, founded in 1414 by Ahmad Shah I as the royal household's mosque beside Bhadra Fort. Its hall has two rows of domes on 152 pillars, many reused from earlier temples, plus stone jali windows.
address: Southwest of Bhadra Fort, walled city

name: Rani Rupmati Mosque
description: Fifteenth-century Sultanate mosque and tomb complex in Mirzapur named after Rani Rupmati, a queen of Mahmud Begada. It has a high central arch, three main domes joined by a flat roof, carved galleries and minarets shortened by the 1819 earthquake.
address: Mirzapur, near St. Xavier's School, Ahmedabad

name: Shah-e-Alam Roza
description: Dargah and mosque complex for the 15th-century Sufi teacher Shah-e-Alam, whose multi-domed tomb with pierced stone screens was completed around 1483. The complex also has a mosque with two minarets, an assembly hall, gateways and a reservoir.
address: Shah Alam, Ahmedabad

name: Dariya Khan's Tomb (Dariya Khan Ghummat)
description: Large brick tomb from 1453 in Shahibaug built for Dariya Khan, a noble of the Gujarat Sultanate. It is the only all-brick tomb in Ahmedabad, with walls about nine feet thick and a big central dome ringed by sixteen smaller ones.
address: Shahibaug, Ahmedabad

name: Azam Khan Sarai
description: Mughal-era building inside the Bhadra Fort complex, built in 1637 by governor Azam Khan as a rest house for travellers and later used as a hospital and jail. Its octagonal entrance hall and a north-wing room turned into a Bhadra Kali shrine survive; it now houses offices including a post office.
address: Bhadra Fort complex, walled city

name: Muhafiz Khan Mosque
description: A small Gujarat Sultanate-era mosque completed in 1465 by governor Jamal-ud-din Muhafiz Khan, known for its three arched entrances and two richly carved 15 m minarets. It is a Monument of National Importance and was restored after damage in 2002.

name: Bhadrakali Temple
description: One of Ahmedabad's oldest temples, dedicated to Ma Bhadrakali, regarded as the city's guardian goddess; it occupies a room in the north wing of Bhadra Fort converted to a temple under Maratha rule. It is especially busy during Navratri.
address: Bhadra Fort, near Manek Chowk, Old City

name: Jagannath Temple, Ahmedabad
description: A Hindu temple to Lord Jagannath in the Jamalpur area of the old city, best known as the starting point of the city's large annual Rath Yatra chariot procession, which travels about 14 km through Ahmedabad.
address: Jamalpur, Ahmedabad

name: Shree Camp Hanuman Temple
description: A temple to Hanuman inside the Ahmedabad Cantonment at Shahibaug, said to be about 250 years old and housing an idol believed to be self-manifested; it is closely associated with army personnel.
address: Ahmedabad Cantonment, Shahibaug

name: ISKCON Temple Ahmedabad (Sri Sri Radha Govind Dham)
description: A Vaishnav temple of the Hare Krishna movement built in 1997 and dedicated to Radha and Krishna (Radha Govindji), combining Hindu temple architecture with Rajasthani styles. It also runs daily scripture classes and celebrates Janmashtami and Ratha-Yatra.
address: Satellite Road, near S.G. Highway, Satellite

name: Vaishno Devi Temple, Ahmedabad
description: A replica of the Vaishno Devi shrine of Jammu and Kashmir, reached by an uphill path lined with garden restaurants, making it a popular family outing on the Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar road.
address: Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar road (S.G. Highway)

name: Adalaj Trimandir
description: A non-sectarian temple complex founded on the teachings of Dada Bhagwan that brings Jain, Shaivite and Vaishnavite deities onto one platform, centred on a 155-inch marble idol of Simandhar Swami, with gardens, a museum and children's theme shows.
address: Near Adalaj village, Ahmedabad-Kalol Highway

name: Swaminarayan Akshardham, Gandhinagar
description: A large BAPS temple complex inaugurated in 1992, whose central mandir is built from about 6,000 tonnes of pink Rajasthani sandstone without steel, with 97 carved pillars; the campus also has exhibitions, the Nilkanth Vatika and an evening water show.
address: Sector 20, 'J' Road, Gandhinagar 382020

name: Mahatma Mandir
description: A convention and exhibition centre in Gandhinagar inspired by Mahatma Gandhi's life, built from 2010, which hosts events such as the Vibrant Gujarat summits; its salt-mound-shaped dome houses the Dandi Kutir museum on Gandhi's life.
address: Sector 13, Gandhinagar

name: Atal Bridge
description: A 300 m kite-inspired steel pedestrian bridge across the Sabarmati between Ellis Bridge and Sardar Bridge, opened in August 2022, with glass floor panels, seating, food kiosks and LED lighting at night.
address: Sabarmati Riverfront (between Ellis Bridge and Sardar Bridge)

name: Narendra Modi Stadium
description: A cricket stadium at Motera, owned by the Gujarat Cricket Association, with a listed capacity of about 132,000; it replaced the old Sardar Patel Stadium and was renamed from Motera Stadium in 2021.
address: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Sports Enclave, Motera

name: Gujarat Vidyapith
description: A university founded by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920 during the non-cooperation movement and a deemed university since 1963, where Gandhian values like dignity of labour and khadi remain part of campus life.
address: Near Income Tax Office, Ashram Road, Ahmedabad 380009

name: Amdavad ni Gufa
description: An underground art gallery designed by architect B. V. Doshi to display works by M. F. Husain, completed in 1995, with mosaic-covered ferro-cement domes and cave-like interiors; it also has a temporary exhibition gallery and a cafe.
address: CEPT campus, University Road (opp. Gujarat University)

name: Calico Museum of Textiles
description: A museum of Indian textiles founded in 1949 by Gautam and Gira Sarabhai and housed since the 1980s in the Sarabhai family's Retreat estate in Shahibaug, showing court textiles, embroideries, tie-dye, temple hangings and religious art through guided tours.
address: The Retreat, Sarabhai Foundation, Shahibaug, Ahmedabad 380004

name: Auto World Vintage Car Museum
description: A large private collection of vintage and classic cars at the Dastan estate on the eastern edge of the city, including Rolls-Royce, Bentley, Mercedes and Cadillac models, plus vintage motorbikes and carriages; managed by the Vintage and Classic Car Club of India.
address: Dastan Estate, Sardar Patel Ring Road, via Naroda-Kathwada Road, Kathwada 382430

name: Lokayatan Folk Museum (Shreyas Folk Museum)
description: A folk art museum founded in 1977 in the landscaped grounds of the Shreyas Foundation, displaying Gujarati woodcarving, metalwork, embroidered textiles, tie-dyed quilts and musical instruments; the ticket also covers the nearby Kalpana Mangaldas children's museum.
address: Bhudarpura, Ahmedabad (Shreyas Foundation grounds)

name: Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Museum (L. D. Institute of Indology)
description: Museum on the L. D. Institute of Indology campus, in a building designed by Balkrishna Doshi, showing Indian sculpture, bronzes, coins, woodwork and a notable collection of Jain manuscripts and paintings across several themed galleries.
address: L. D. Institute of Indology campus, opp. Gujarat University, Navrangpura, Ahmedabad 380009

name: N. C. Mehta Gallery
description: Gallery wing of the L. D. Museum holding the N. C. Mehta collection of over 1,200 Indian miniature paintings, including Jain, Rajasthani, Mughal and Pahari works and an early Gita Govinda series; a few hundred are on display at a time.
address: Premises of the L. D. Institute of Indology, next to Gujarat University, Navrangpura, Ahmedabad

name: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Memorial
description: Museum in the Mughal-era Moti Shahi Mahal in Shahibaug, built for Shah Jahan, presenting the life and work of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel with portraits and personal items, plus a room on Gandhi and a room remembering Rabindranath Tagore's stay.
address: Moti Shahi Mahal, Shahibaug, near Civil Hospital, Ahmedabad

name: Vechaar Utensils Museum
description: Museum of traditional kitchen utensils founded in 1981 by Surendra Patel inside the Vishalla village-style restaurant, displaying over 4,500 vessels and tools in brass, copper, bronze, clay and other materials, with open displays rather than glass cases.
address: Inside Vishalla, opp. APMC Market, Vishalla Circle, Sarkhej-Vasna road, Ahmedabad 380055

name: Tribal Museum (Tribal Research and Training Institute, Gujarat Vidyapith)
description: Museum of the Tribal Research and Training Institute (founded 1962) at Gujarat Vidyapith, laid out like tribal homes and showing dress, crafts, jewellery, tools and a large photo collection documenting the tribal communities of Gujarat.
address: Gujarat Vidyapith, Ashram Road, Ahmedabad 380014

name: Conflictorium
description: Small two-storey museum opened in 2013 in the old Gool Lodge building in Mirzapur that uses participatory art installations and exhibits to explore conflict, memory and constitutional values.
address: Gool Lodge, opp. R.C. High School of Commerce, Delhi Chakla, Mirzapur, Ahmedabad 380001

name: Kanoria Centre for Arts
description: Non-profit arts centre founded in 1984 by Urmila Kanoria with support from B. V. Doshi, with the Urmila Art Gallery, the Urmila Kailash Black Box, artists' studios, an art shop, a library and a cafe.
address: Opp. Gujarat University, University Road, Navrangpura, Ahmedabad 380009

name: Dandi Kutir Museum
description: Salt-mound-shaped museum in Gandhinagar on the life and ideas of Mahatma Gandhi, using audio-visual shows, 3-D and 360-degree projections and interactive displays; run by the state Archaeology and Museums office since 2015.
address: Gandhinagar

name: Gandhi Smarak Sangrahalaya
description: Museum within Sabarmati (Gandhi) Ashram designed by Charles Correa and opened in 1963, holding letters, manuscripts, photographs and books by and about Mahatma Gandhi in modular pavilions around a water court.
address: Gandhi Ashram, Ahmedabad 380027

name: Kankaria Lake
description: Large 15th-century artificial lake in Maninagar with an island garden, Nagina Wadi, reached by a causeway; its lakefront has walking paths, a toy train, a tethered balloon, boating, play areas and food stalls, and hosts the annual Kankaria Carnival in late December.
address: Kankaria, Maninagar, Ahmedabad 380008

name: Kamla Nehru Zoological Garden, Kankaria
description: City zoo founded in 1951 beside Kankaria Lake on about 117 acres, housing mammals, birds and reptiles and known for conservation breeding of rare species.
address: Kankaria, Maninagar, Ahmedabad

name: Butterfly Park, Kankaria
description: Open-air butterfly garden at One Tree Hill near Kankaria Lake, part of the lakefront attractions, with host plants and an interpretation centre explaining the butterfly life cycle.
address: One Tree Hill Garden, Kankaria, Ahmedabad

name: Nocturnal Zoo, Kamla Nehru Zoological Garden
description: Night-house exhibit at the Kankaria zoo, built in 2017, where dim lighting lets visitors see night-active animals such as hedgehogs, jungle cats and striped hyenas.
address: Kamla Nehru Zoological Garden, Kankaria, Ahmedabad

name: Riverfront Flower Park
description: Flower garden of about 3.85 hectares on the Sabarmati Riverfront near Ellisbridge, opened in 2016, with themed beds of many native and exotic species and the venue of Ahmedabad's annual flower show.
address: Sabarmati Riverfront, near Ellisbridge, Ahmedabad

name: Sabarmati Riverfront Lower Promenade (West bank)
description: Riverside pedestrian and cycling walkway on the west bank of the Sabarmati, part of the riverfront's lower promenade of roughly 11 km per bank running just above water level, with ghats giving access to the river.
address: Sabarmati Riverfront, west bank, Ahmedabad

name: Sabarmati Riverfront Lower Promenade (East bank)
description: Riverside pedestrian and cycling walkway on the east bank of the Sabarmati, mirroring the west-bank promenade, running just above water level with ghats and views across to the western city.
address: Sabarmati Riverfront, east bank, Ahmedabad

name: Vastrapur Lake (Bhakta Kavi Narsinh Mehta Lake)
description: Municipal lake in western Ahmedabad, officially Bhakta Kavi Narsinh Mehta Lake, ringed by lawns, stonework gardens, an open-air theatre, a children's park and a walking path around the water; redeveloped and reopened with paid entry from January 2026.
address: Vastrapur, Ahmedabad

name: Parimal Garden
description: Municipal park in Ambawadi, established in 1960 and restored by the Torrent Group (reopened 2022), with a central lotus pond, walkways, a herbal garden, lawns, a yoga pavilion, a pet park and an amphitheatre.
address: Ambawadi, Ahmedabad

name: Law Garden (Sheth Motilal Hirabhai Park)
description: Ten-acre public park in Navrangpura with lawns, fountains, a pond, a children's play area and a jogging track; the road beside it hosts evening street stalls and the Happy Street food court.
address: Opp. Gujarat Law Society, Navrangpura (Ellisbridge), Ahmedabad

name: Chandola Lake
description: A large circular embanked reservoir near Dani Limda in south Ahmedabad, fed by the old Kharicut Canal and known for waterbirds such as cormorants, painted storks and spoonbills. After encroachments were cleared in 2025, the state approved a phased plan to beautify the lake.
address: Dani Limda Road, Ahmedabad

name: Sundarvan
description: A small nature park and recognised mini-zoo next to SAC-ISRO, created in 1978 from a former mango orchard, with tree groves, ponds for birdwatching, reptiles, birds, butterflies and fish. The Centre for Environment Education runs it and holds regular snake-awareness demonstrations.
address: Next to SAC-ISRO, Satellite Road, Ahmedabad

name: Indroda Nature Park (Indroda Dinosaur and Fossil Park)
description: A large eco-education park on the Sabarmati in Gandhinagar, managed by the GEER Foundation. It combines a dinosaur and fossil park with a zoo, botanical garden, aviary, butterfly park, reptile house and natural history museum.
address: Sector 7, Gandhinagar (near CH-0 circle)

name: Sarita Udyan
description: A popular flower garden in Sector 9 of Gandhinagar on the banks of the Sabarmati River, suited to strolling and relaxing, with a deer park close by.
address: Sector 9, Gandhinagar

name: Punit Van
description: A botanical garden in Sector 19, Gandhinagar, laid out by the Gujarat forest department in 2005. Its roughly 3,500 trees are grouped into themed sections linked to stars, planets and zodiac signs, such as Nakshatra Van, Rashi Van, Nav Grah Van and Panchvati Van.
address: Sector 19, Gandhinagar

name: Gujarat Science City
description: A large science education and entertainment campus off S.G. Highway run by the Gujarat Council of Science City. It has halls of science and space, robotics, aquatic and astronomy galleries, energy and life science parks, a nature park and an IMAX 3D theatre.
address: Science City Road, off S. G. Highway, Ahmedabad 380060

name: Kids City, Kankaria Lakefront
description: A miniature role-play town for children at Kankaria Lakefront with about 18 activity centres, including a bank, fire station, radio station, court room and hospital, where kids try out grown-up jobs. In October 2026 AMC approved new attractions and an upgrade of existing activities.
address: Kankaria Lakefront, Maninagar, Ahmedabad

name: Atal Express (Kankaria toy train)
description: A toy train that circles Kankaria Lake on a 4.5 km track at about 10 km/h, carrying up to 150 passengers. Opened on 25 December 2008 and named after Atal Bihari Vajpayee, it runs from the child-friendly area of the lakefront.
address: Kankaria Lakefront, Maninagar, Ahmedabad

name: Balvatika, Kankaria
description: A children's park near Kankaria Zoo, first opened in 1956 and named after Jawaharlal Nehru, reopened in July 2025 after redevelopment. It now has a glass selfie tower, mirror maze, dinosaur park, wax museum, illusion house, snow park, go-karting and other rides.
address: Kankaria Lakefront, Maninagar, Ahmedabad

name: Kankaria Lake Boating (Naginawadi)
description: Boating on Kankaria Lake run by AMC from Naginawadi, with options such as pedal and motor boats, shikara, kayak, speed boat, jet ski and a floating café. Boating resumed on 1 November 2025.
address: Naginawadi, Kankaria Lakefront, Ahmedabad

name: Morning Heritage Walk (AMC)
description: A guided morning walk through Ahmedabad's walled city organised by the municipal corporation, starting at the Kalupur Swaminarayan Temple and ending at Jama Masjid. It takes in temples, mosques, carved wooden houses and the old pol neighbourhoods.
address: Starts at Swaminarayan Temple, Kalupur; ends at Jama Masjid

name: Akshar River Cruise (Sabarmati Riverfront)
description: A restaurant cruise on the Sabarmati River at the Riverfront, offering lunch and dinner sailings of about an hour and a half. It was launched in 2023 under the Sabarmati Riverfront Development project, with an offline ticket counter under Atal Bridge.
address: Sabarmati Riverfront, reception under Atal Bridge, Ahmedabad

name: Sat-Chit-Anand Water Show, Swaminarayan Akshardham
description: An outdoor evening show at Akshardham, Gandhinagar, that retells the Kathopanishad story of young Nachiketa and Yama using a water screen, lasers, projections, fire, fountains and surround sound. It is performed in Hindi and can be cancelled in rain.
address: Swaminarayan Akshardham, Sector 20, J Road, Gandhinagar 382020

name: Law Garden Night Market
description: An evening street market along the side road of Law Garden (Sheth Motilal Hirabhai Park) in Navrangpura, known for ethnic clothes, jewellery and handicrafts, plus a food street revamped in 2020 as 'Happy Street'.
address: Law Garden, Navrangpura, Ahmedabad

name: Lal Darwaja Market
description: A busy street market in the old city around Lal Darwaja near Bhadra, close to the Sidi Saiyyed Mosque, selling traditional clothes, handicrafts, toys, jewellery, electronics and books, with street-food stalls nearby.
address: Lal Darwaja, Bhadra, Old City, Ahmedabad

name: Dhalgarwad Market
description: A busy textile and clothing market near Bhadra Plaza in the old city, known for affordable sarees, children's wear, cotton fabrics, Rajasthani prints and cloth sold by the metre, with tailors and embroidery machines in its lanes.
address: Near Bhadra Plaza, Old City, Ahmedabad

name: Teen Darwaza Market
description: A busy street market around Teen Darwaza, the 15th-century triple gateway east of Bhadra Fort in the old city. Stalls sell clothing, footwear, household goods, embroidered items and curios, alongside street snacks such as panipuri and dabeli.
address: Teen Darwaza, near Bhadra Fort, Old City

name: Sindhi Market (Revdi Bazar)
description: A wholesale-and-retail market in the old city next to Kalupur Gate, also called Revdi Bazar. It is known for fabrics, bedsheets, footwear, carpets, handicrafts and upholstery materials.
address: Next to Kalupur Gate, Old City

name: Ahmedabad Haat (Vastrapur Haat)
description: An open crafts bazaar in Vastrapur for handloom and handicrafts such as embroidered dress material, Kutch and Jamnagar bandhani and mirror-work garments, with folk dancers and drummers performing. It also hosts seasonal exhibition-cum-sale fairs.
address: Vastrapur

name: Ravivari (Sunday Market)
description: A centuries-old Sunday flea market (Gujari Bazaar), said to date from 1414 under Sultan Ahmad Shah and held on the Sabarmati riverfront near Ellisbridge since 1954. Hundreds of stalls sell second-hand goods, clothes, books, tools, antiques and household items.
address: Sabarmati riverfront, Ellisbridge (behind Gaikwad Haveli, near Sardar Bridge)

name: C. G. Road (Chimanlal Girdharlal Road)
description: A major city road running from Mahalaxmi Crossroads to Sardar Patel Stadium Crossroads, linking Paldi and Navrangpura. Redesigned in the 1990s, it is a financial hub and ranked as the city's costliest retail location, lined with shops and showrooms.
address: Mahalaxmi Crossroads to Sardar Patel Stadium Crossroads, Navrangpura

name: Ahmedabad One (formerly Alpha One)
description: A large mixed-use mall near Vastrapur Lake that opened in October 2011, with about 708,000 sq ft of retail over three floors, department-store anchors, a six-screen multiplex and a top-floor food court.
address: Plot No-216, near Vastrapur Lake, Vastrapur, Ahmedabad 380054

name: Palladium Ahmedabad
description: A luxury mall on the Sarkhej-Gandhinagar Highway in Thaltej, opened in February 2023 by BSafal and The Phoenix Mills. It spans about 750,000 sq ft over five floors with 250-plus brands, two floors of dining, a nine-screen PVR and play arcades.
address: Sarkhej-Gandhinagar Highway, Thaltej

name: Manek Chowk (jewellery / bullion market)
description: Manek Chowk, a historic square in the walled city named after saint Baba Maneknath, turns from a morning vegetable market into a bullion and jewellery market around midday, reported as one of the largest in India.
address: Manek Chowk, walled city, near Bhadra Fort

name: Relief Road
description: A historic commercial street through the old city (Panchkuva, Zaveriwad and Kalupur areas) lined with shops selling textiles, traditional wear, electronics, household goods and second-hand books.
address: Old City (Panchkuva / Zaveriwad / Kalupur)

name: Manek Chowk Night Market
description: After the jewellery shops close, food stalls with tables and chairs fill the old-city square every night, serving sweets and savoury snacks such as pav bhaji, sandwiches and dosa; it is especially known for rabri kulfi.
address: Manek Chowk, Old City

name: Vishalla
description: A village-style Gujarati restaurant opened in 1978, where diners sit on the floor and eat thali from leaf plates in an open-air rustic setting. The site also houses the Vechaar Utensils Museum of traditional vessels.
address: Opp. APMC Market, Vishalla Circle, Vasna, Ahmedabad 380055

name: Agashiye, The House of MG
description: A rooftop restaurant on The House of MG, a 1924 heritage haveli in the old city, serving a fixed daily-changing vegetarian Gujarati thali since 1999, with starters on the terrace.
address: The House of MG, Opp. Sidi Saiyad Jali, Lal Darwaja, Ahmedabad 380001

name: Gordhan Thal
description: A Gujarati thali restaurant serving a hearty unlimited-style spread of savoury and sweet dishes brought to the table.
address: Sapath Complex, opp. Rajpath Club, S.G. Highway, Bodakdev

name: Swati Snacks (Law Garden)
description: Casual vegetarian restaurant from a Mumbai brand founded over 50 years ago, serving home-style Gujarati dishes and street-food favourites such as handvo, patra and dhokla.
address: Panchavati Road, Law Garden, Ahmedabad 380006

name: Das Khaman
description: A khaman shop founded in 1922 by Pitambardas Thakkar ('Das') opposite the municipal office in Bhadra, now run by the family's fourth generation and known for steamed chickpea-flour khaman variants. Sardar Patel was a regular.
address: Surendra Mangaldas Road, Bhadra

name: Rajwadu
description: A sprawling village-themed restaurant styled like a fortified Gujarat-Rajasthan village, with stone walls, courtyards, gardens, water features and folk performers, serving Gujarati, Kathiawadi and Rajasthani thalis and snacks.
address: Near Jivraj Tolnaka, Ambaji Temple, Malav Talav, Vejalpur

name: Lucky Restaurant (Lucky Tea Stall)
description: A decades-old tea stall turned eatery near Lal Darwaja, famous for tables set among old graves inside the dining room and for an M.F. Husain painting the artist gave the owner in 1994. Known for chai and bun-maska.
address: Mirzapur Road, Lal Darwaja

name: Patang Re-Evolve (Patang Hotel revolving restaurant)
description: Revolving fine-dining restaurant atop the 1984 Patang Hotel tower designed by Hasmukh Patel, turning a full circle in about 90 minutes with panoramic city views; it reopened in October 2023 after renovation and seats up to 110 guests.
address: Nehru Bridge corner, Ashram Road, Ahmedabad 380009

name: Chandravilas Restaurant
description: Ahmedabad's oldest well-known eatery, founded in 1900 by Chimanlal Joshi on Gandhi Road in the old city; credited with introducing the Gujarati thali to the city and famous for fafda-jalebi.
address: Gandhi Road, Khadia, Ahmedabad

name: Iscon Gathiya
description: Long-running farsan shop where diners stand at steel tables eating gathiya, fafda, cold jalebi and free kadhi with chutneys; a popular breakfast stop.
address: Opposite Karnavati Club, S G Highway, Satellite, Ahmedabad

name: Sasuji
description: Gujarati thali restaurant on C G Road focused on traditional, milder home-style flavours, with food served at the table onto large thalis; also noted for farsan and kadhi.
address: Lal Bunglow, Singaporean Avenue, C G Road, Navrangpura, Ahmedabad 380009

name: Pakwan Dining Hall
description: Pure-vegetarian dining hall serving traditional Gujarati thali meals with rotis, puris, rice, dal, vegetables and farsan.
address: S G Highway at Bodakdev Road, Ahmedabad 380058

name: Qutbuddin Mosque
description: 15th-century Sultanate mosque near Delhi Gate in the old city, attributed to Sultan Qutb-ud-din Ahmad Shah II, with five large domes on sixty pillars, marble mihrabs and Hindu-temple-style carved buttresses; partly ruined, it is a Monument of National Importance.
address: Old city, about 270 m from Delhi Gate, Ahmedabad

name: Haibat Khan's Mosque
description: Early Sultanate mosque built in 1412 by Haibat Khan, uncle of Ahmed Shah I, near Jamalpur gate; one of the first attempts to blend Islamic and Hindu temple architecture, with a plain three-arched front, two small minarets and a carved central dome.
address: Near Jamalpur Gate, Ahmedabad

name: Malik Alam's Mosque
description: Mosque built in 1422 by Malik Alam, son-in-law of Sultan Ahmed Shah I, in the Shah Alam area; it has five domes, five marble mihrabs and earthquake-damaged minarets, and stands partly ruined as a Monument of National Importance.
address: Shah Alam area, Ahmedabad

name: Saiyad Usman Mosque (Sayyid Usman Roza)
description: Sufi mosque and tomb complex in Usmanpura built by Sultan Mahmud Begada around 1460 for the saint Saiyid Usman; the tomb's dome rests on twelve pillars and the style resembles the Sarkhej Roza tombs. It is a Monument of National Importance.
address: Usmanpura, Ahmedabad

name: Gita Mandir
description: Krishna temple founded in 1940 by Swami Vidyanandji Maharaj, enshrining a Krishna idol with an image of Gita Mata, with Bhagavad Gita verses on marble wall panels; it heads a trust of Gita Mandirs and gives its name to the road and adjoining central bus station.
address: Gita Mandir Road, Jamalpur, Ahmedabad (beside the central bus station)

name: Delhi Darwaja (Delhi Gate)
description: Three-arched stone gateway in the north wall of the old walled city, built in the Sultanate era under Mahmud Begada and once known as Idariyo Darwajo; side openings for pedestrians were added in 1878, and carved elephants and lions decorate it.
address: Delhi Darwaja, old city, Ahmedabad (near Shahibaug and Hutheesing Jain Temple)

name: Astodia Darwaza (Astodia Gate)
description: South-eastern gate of the old walled city, part of the second fort completed under Mahmud Begada; built of dressed ashlar stone with three arches and lotus medallions, it now stands as a traffic island on the main road.
address: Astodia, old city, Ahmedabad (near Dhal-ni-Pol and Rani Sipri's tomb)

name: Lokmanya Tilak Bag (Victoria Garden)
description: Colonial-era public park at the east end of Ellis Bridge, opened in 1905 and formerly named for a Queen Victoria statue now kept at Sanskar Kendra; it has old trees, fountains, play areas, a Tilak statue unveiled by Gandhi in 1929, and the Sunday Ravivari market nearby.
address: Near Swami Vivekanand (Ellis) Bridge, Lal Darwaja, Old City, Ahmedabad 380001

name: Children's Park, Gandhinagar
description: City park in Sector 28 of Gandhinagar with a lake and boating, a mini train for children, a separate gaming zone and garden lawns, popular for evening walks and picnics.
address: Sector 28, Gandhinagar

name: Aquatic Gallery, Gujarat Science City
description: Large public aquarium at Gujarat Science City, opened in July 2021, holding about 11,690 animals of 188 species in 68 tanks grouped by world region, with a 28-metre shark tunnel.
address: Gujarat Science City, Science City Road, Ahmedabad

name: Robotics Gallery, Gujarat Science City
description: Three-floor robotics exhibition at Gujarat Science City, opened in July 2021, displaying about 200 robots of 79 types, including dancing humanoids, robot fights, robot soccer and badminton, plus VR and interactive exhibits.
address: Gujarat Science City, Science City Road, Ahmedabad
